A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamicCut/DynamicCutMix study. Their complete 22-page contents, including Appendices A–C, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original memorization analyses, sample-removal experiments, generative-model comparisons, and appendix ablations and evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–6 and Appendix A, including benchmark comparisons and memorization-tag prediction results.

M1.justification: DynamicCut retains early Mem-AUC scoring, top-epoch pooling, sample filtering, and retraining. DynamicCutMix remains its combination with TabCutMix; no algorithm or architecture change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult, Default, and Shoppers, plus Cardio and Wilt in Appendix A.2. Data-generation and downstream classification task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TabDDPM, CTGAN, TVAE, and the SMOTE, TCM, and TCMP augmentation baselines. Comparator membership is unchanged in the main experiments and Appendix A.

E3.justification: Both retain the same synthetic-sample counts, memorization threshold, evaluation metrics, and reported dataset splits. Table 10 is relocated without changing its sample counts or split information.

E4.justification: The removal controls, memorization and forgetting analyses, tag-ratio and pooling ablations, transferability studies, case examples, and generation-quality checks remain unchanged in Sections 3–6 and Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both specify averaging over five independent experimental runs in Section 6.1. The tables retain the same ± reporting, and Appendix C.4 retains the fixed-seed splitting statement.

E6.justification: Result entries, numerical values, and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 reports the same Default TabDDPM+DCM memorization ratio of 15.79±2.06% in both versions.

T1.justification: The relative-distance ratio, memorization and forgetting event definitions, Mem-AUC integrals, and filtering-score definitions are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.3. No theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim and contributions concerning concentrated early memorization, model-agnostic mitigation, preservation of data quality, and transfer across generative models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of memorization dynamics and utility tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning monitoring overhead, late-emerging memorization, and sensitivity to warm-up and filtering hyperparameters.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly provides an anonymous DynamicCut code-repository URL. This adds documented code-access information; the framework, optimizer, and other implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds four works: Somepalli et al. (2023b), Wen et al. (2024), Hintersdorf et al. (2024), and Shah et al. (2025). The Jinsung Yoon et al. (2023a) citation and reference are removed. The substantive research-gap and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited wording and spacing edits accompany citation updates. Appendix A.6.1 corrects its heatmap reference from Figure 11 to Figure 10, and Appendix C.4 replaces Table ?? with Table 10. The section structure and narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 10 moves from PDF page 22 to page 21, retaining its caption, structure, and values. Other visual differences are localized text and reference reflow. All eleven figure graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer in Appendix C improves access documentation, while correcting the wrong figure reference and unresolved table reference improves navigation. These resolve limited documentation defects. The method, experimental evidence, and substantive discussion remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is modest.
